h1: Hydraulic presses — shop presses, H-frame, C-frame and production presses
intro: A hydraulic press machine does the pressing, forming, drawing and straightening work of every repair shop, fabricator and production plant: a hydraulic shop press (H-frame press) presses bearings and pins, straightens shafts and bends plate, and a production press runs a die — forming, deep drawing, blanking, moulding — cycle after cycle under PLC control. Both lines are on this page, small to large. The workshop presses come first: DPM shop presses from 33 to 220 US tons with two-speed joystick control, the DPM-K and DK with a cylinder that travels across the frame, the AT T-slot die presses, the AP garage press brake and the DK-S 3-axis straightening presses to 441 US tons. Below them, NovoTech's premium line of production hydraulic presses, built in Turkey with European components: HSA single action and HDD double action deep drawing H-frame presses to 3,307 US tons, HCFP column presses, CFS, CFSS and CFDD C-frame presses, SMC / HHRP hot plate presses for composites and rubber, HSPS portal straightening presses and the HDT Eco H-frame. Every press with a CSA-approved panel, pressure gauge and relief valve, parts and service in Canada.

faq.q: What tonnage shop press do I need?
faq.a: Most truck, equipment and fabrication shops run a 66 – 110 US ton press (DPM 1040-60 to DPM 1570-100): enough for pressing bearings and bushings, straightening shafts to Ø3″ and bending flat bar. Go to 165 – 220 US tons for large bearings, track pins, heavy shafts and forming plate; the DK-S straightening presses from 220 to 441 US tons are for plates, beams and bar that need a moving ram.

faq.q: What do the model numbers mean — DPM 1040-60?
faq.a: The first number is the clear working width between the columns in millimetres (1040 mm = 40.9″) and the second the press force in metric tons (60 t = 66 US tons). A 1570-100 press is 61.8″ wide at 110 US tons.

On the DPM-K and DK the cylinder head travels across the frame on a hand wheel, so the ram comes to the work — a long shaft, a frame rail or a plate stays clamped while you straighten it point by point instead of shifting the part under a fixed ram. The DK series adds a wider 61.8″ – 74.8″ frame.

faq.q: Can a shop press bend plate?
faq.a: The AP garage-type press brake is a hydraulic press delivered with a 5-face prism bottom die and hardened top blade for bending 1/4″ (110 US tons) or 3/8″ (165 US tons) mild steel over 40″ or 60″ — the economical way to bend brackets and short plate without a full press brake. The AT press has T-slot tables for bolting your own forming, blanking and coining dies.

faq.q: Hand pump, foot pedal or two-hand control?
faq.a: The DPM and DPM-K presses come with two-speed joystick control; a hand pump for fine pressing, a foot pedal and a limit switch that stops the stroke at a set height are options. The AT and AP presses are two-hand controlled with stepless stroke adjustment by limit switch, as die and bending work requires.

A shop press is operated by hand — joystick or two-hand buttons — for one part at a time: pressing, straightening, bending. A production press runs a die under PLC control with programmed speeds, pressures, dwell and return, light barriers instead of guards, automatic lubrication and remote diagnostics, for thousands of cycles a shift. The NovoTech premium line starts at 33 US tons with the CFS C-frame and goes to 3,307 US tons on the H-frame presses.

faq.q: Single action or double action — what is a die cushion?
faq.a: A single action press has one ram. A double action (deep drawing) press adds a die cushion in the lower table — a second cylinder that holds the blank holder with its own programmed force — so a flat blank can be drawn into a deep cup, pan or housing without wrinkling. The HDD H-frame and CFDD C-frame presses have the cushion built in; it is an option on the HCFP column press.

An H-frame (straight-side) press is the stiffest and takes the largest tables and tonnages — the choice for deep drawing and big dies. A column (four-post) press is open on all sides for die access and automation. A C-frame press is open on three sides, so small dies go in and out quickly and the press takes less floor space; its table size is limited because the C deflects, which is why the C-frame range stops at 276 US tons.

faq.q: Can the press be built to my die?
faq.a: Yes — every series of the premium line is built to order in the table size, stroke, daylight and tonnage the die needs, from a 33 US ton C-frame to a 3,307 US ton H-frame, with quick die change, die loading arms, ejector, heated platens or a die cushion as required. Send us the die drawing and the cycle you need and we quote the press around it.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
